en: The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan originated from the literal practice of an entire community physically carrying a family's nipa hut to a new location.
Dr. Fe del Mundo, the first Asian admitted to Harvard Medical School, invented a makeshift bamboo incubator to keep premature babies warm without electricity.
The original 1898 Philippine Declaration of Independence was handwritten in Spanish by lawyer Ambrosio Rianzares Bautista, not in the native Tagalog language.
General Gregorio del Pilar became the youngest general in the Philippine Revolutionary Army at just twenty-four years old before dying heroically at the Battle of Tirad Pass.
Before the Spanish arrived, literate Filipinos wrote their native languages using the Baybayin alphabet by carving letters directly onto bamboo tubes and palm leaves.
The Philippine Eagle, our national bird, possesses a unique crest of long, dark brown feathers that makes its head look remarkably like a lion's mane.
The indigenous Ifugao people carved the massive Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains over two thousand years ago using only simple hand tools and zero modern machinery.
During the Lucban Pahiyas Festival, locals decorate their house exteriors with kiping, which are vibrant, leaf-shaped wafers made entirely from ground rice and food coloring.
The lyrics of Lupang Hinirang were originally written in Spanish as Filipinas by soldier Jose Palma in 1899, eight years after Julian Felipe composed the music.
National Artist Napoleon Abueva, known as the Father of Modern Philippine Sculpture, carved his first major masterpiece out of molave wood when he was only nineteen.
Gabriela Silang was the first Filipina to lead a revolt against Spanish rule, taking over her executed husband's army and leading them in battle.
The iconic Philippine jeepney was originally created by modifying surplus American military jeeps left behind in the country after the end of World War II.
